meetings.title: Kickoff for the loyalty app relaunch
meetings.overview: The team starts the relaunch of the loyalty app. They set the launch date, the budget and the first owners.
keyPoints: Quillpay stays as payment provider for now
decisions: Keep Quillpay as the payment provider for launch
Launch on 14 March

actions.task: Get legal sign-off on the privacy label

openQuestions: How long do loyalty points last?

say.text: Okay, let's start. This is the kickoff for the loyalty app relaunch. The goal is a launch on 14 March.
14 March works for QA if we freeze features by 20 February. I will lead QA for the whole run.
Good. The budget is 120k for the full relaunch, and that includes the payment work.
For payments I suggest we keep Quillpay. We already have the contract and the team knows the API.
I agree. Changing providers now would cost us weeks, and I want the design work to start soon.
Then the decision is simple. Quillpay stays for launch.
I will book six test devices this week. I will also set up a crash dashboard so we see problems early.
On my side I need to finish the icon set. We have forty icons and I want them done by 12 January.
Priyanka, what do we need for the store?
Mainly the privacy label for the app store. I will ask legal for a sign-off, and I will start with the data map.
Fine. Another thing. How long do loyalty points last before they expire?
Nobody knows yet. Finance has not told us. Put it as an open question.
We should also think about guest checkout. Many shoppers want to pay without an account.
Yes, keep guest checkout in scope for now. We will look at it again.
I also want a weekly meeting, same day, thirty minutes.
Agreed. Next meeting in one week.

meetings.title: Store prerequisites check
meetings.overview: The team reviews the store submission checklist. Several items still wait on other teams. Guest checkout work is paused.
keyPoints: Privacy label review is still pending
A crash on older Android devices is under study
decisions: Guest checkout work is paused for now

actions.task: Get legal sign-off on the privacy label
Buy two more Android phones for the lab

openQuestions: How long do loyalty points last?
Who pays for the extra phones?

say.text: Let's go through the store checklist. Priyanka, where is the privacy label?
Still waiting for legal. They have a backlog of twelve days, so the review will not finish before 2 February.
That is late. Please keep pushing them, and tell me if it slips again.
On crashes, I found one on Android 11. The app closes when a user opens the points screen after a login.
I cannot reproduce it well, because we have only two Android 11 phones in the lab. I will ask for a few more.
I finished the release notes draft yesterday. I put it in the shared folder.
Thanks. And the icon set, Sunniva?
Twenty-six of forty are done. I will finish the rest by 19 January.
Another thing. The push notification certificate must be renewed. I will take that one myself.
Do we know when it expires?
On 3 December, so we still have time, but not a lot.
Now about guest checkout. I want to drop it from the first release. Let's pause the work on it.
I am fine with pausing. It saves test effort.
I have a feeling it hurts us, but I need data first.
We pause it. Bring the data next time.
What about points expiry? Do we have an answer from finance?
No answer yet. I will ask them again this week.
Okay. Next week we meet again.

meetings.title: Payment provider change
meetings.overview: The team talks about the payment provider and the store gate. A new provider is chosen. The crash work becomes the top item.
keyPoints: Crash work is now the top item
Terms of service page needs an update
decisions: Move to Tarnbridge Pay; Quillpay stays only for old subscriptions

actions.task: Update the terms of service page

openQuestions: How long do loyalty points last?
Does the new provider need a new contract review?

say.text: Today we talk about payments. Priyanka has news from Quillpay.
Quillpay sent a new price list. The fee goes from 1.8 percent to 2.9 percent from 1 March.
That changes the business case. Tobias, what is the alternative?
Tarnbridge Pay. Their fee is 1.9 percent, and their SDK has a ready receipt module. Migration is about three weeks of work.
Will it delay the launch?
Not if we start now. I would say we move to Tarnbridge and keep Quillpay only for old subscriptions.
Then the decision is to move to Tarnbridge Pay. Tobias owns the migration.
I need to update the terms of service page for the new provider too.
Back to the store submission. The crash rate on Android 11 is 2.8 percent, and our store gate in the checklist is 1 percent.
Then the crash fix is the top item. Tobias, please make it your first task.
About the push certificate. I tried to log in to the Brightline portal, and it is locked until 20 November after a failed login.
So we cannot renew it before then.
Right. I will try again after the lock ends.
For the beta test, I want 200 users. I will prepare the invitations.
Good. Please also finish the icons, Sunniva.
Yes, 34 of 40 are done now.

meetings.title: Guest checkout and sandbox keys
meetings.overview: The team settles guest checkout with data. Payment testing and the certificate still wait on outside parties. Legal review is still running.
keyPoints: Guest checkout stays out of the first release
Payment testing waits on the provider
Crash rate is falling but still high
decisions: Guest checkout stays out of the first release

actions.task: Follow up with Tarnbridge twice a week
Get legal sign-off on the privacy label

openQuestions: How long do loyalty points last?
Is the privacy label ready in time for the store?

say.text: Let's start with guest checkout. Sunniva, you promised numbers.
Here they are. Guest checkout orders have a 31 percent refund rate, and orders with an account have 9 percent. That costs real money.
That is a strong number. It also means more privacy work, because we keep data for people without accounts.
Then guest checkout stays out of the first release. Sunniva will write the refund policy text.
Yes. I will write it this week.
On Tarnbridge, I have bad news. The sandbox keys will only arrive on 19 November, so I cannot test receipts before that.
That is a risk for the submission. Please follow up with them twice a week.
About the push certificate. Brightline says the account admin left the company, and they need a signed letter from a director.
I will ask our director for the letter.
The privacy label is still in the legal queue. They say it is the second item now.
And finance? Did they answer the points expiry question?
Not yet. They said maybe next week.
The crash on Android 11 is down to 1.9 percent after my first fix, but it is still above the gate.
Okay. Keep going.
We also need to pay the icon contractor invoice. I will ask accounts.

meetings.title: Launch date review
meetings.overview: The team moves the launch date and the budget. Roles change, and the payment plan changes again. Many items are still open.
keyPoints: Both payment providers will run together for a while
decisions: Run Quillpay and Tarnbridge in parallel until 30 April
Launch on 2 May

actions.task: Update the terms of service page

openQuestions: How long do loyalty points last?
Can two payment providers run side by side without double charges?

say.text: We need to talk about the launch date. With the late sandbox keys and the crash work, 14 March is not realistic.
I agree. I suggest 2 May. That gives us time for a proper beta.
And the budget? We paid for the provider change and for more test work.
The new budget is 165k. I got approval yesterday.
One more change. Priyanka takes over as QA lead, and Tobias focuses on the Tarnbridge integration.
Fine. I will start by reviewing the open crash list.
For payments, my plan is to run Quillpay and Tarnbridge in parallel until 30 April, then cut over.
Then the decision is a parallel run until 30 April.
The icon contractor stopped work because the invoice of 4,800 is still unpaid. Only 36 icons are done.
I will fix the invoice today.
The push certificate is still open. The signed letter is with our director.
He will sign on Monday. Then I send it to Brightline.
The points expiry is still open. Finance says it is either 18 or 24 months, and the liability figure of 410k depends on it.
That is a big difference. I need that answer before launch.
The beta test needs 200 users. I will send invitations after the crash fix.
Receipts migration is 60 percent done. It waits for the production keys.
Good. Next meeting in two weeks.

meetings.title: Início do projeto RotaViva
meetings.overview: A rede decide trocar as planilhas de entrega por um sistema de rotas. Define-se um piloto, o patrocinador e a data de início.
keyPoints: O projeto substitui as planilhas de rotas das lojas
Início do piloto marcado para fevereiro
Custo mensal do sistema já estimado
decisions: Piloto em três lojas: Centro, Vila Nova e Serra
Início do piloto em 3 de fevereiro
openQuestions: Quem paga o seguro dos tablets?

say.text: Bom dia pessoal. Hoje a gente começa o projeto do RotaViva, que vai trocar as planilhas de entrega por um sistema de rotas.
Eu já falei com o fornecedor. O custo é 4.200 reais por mês para todas as lojas.
Pelo financeiro tá ok, dentro do orçamento do ano. Só preciso do contrato assinado até o fim do mês.
Perfeito. Eu sou o patrocinador do projeto e a Cássia cuida da parte técnica.
Sobre o piloto, eu sugiro três lojas: Centro, Vila Nova e Serra. Assim a gente pega bairros diferentes.
Concordo, três lojas. E quando começa?
Dá para começar em 3 de fevereiro, se os equipamentos chegarem em dezembro.
Quantos equipamentos a gente precisa?
Dezoito tablets, um para cada motoboy do piloto.
Ótimo. Os motoboys precisam de treinamento antes do piloto.
Isso. Eu levanto a lista de bairros esta semana, que já ajuda no treinamento.
E o seguro dos tablets? Alguém já pensou nisso?
Boa pergunta. Vamos deixar em aberto por enquanto.
Anotado.
Então a gente se vê daqui a dez dias.

meetings.title: Equipamentos e modo offline
meetings.overview: A equipe revisa a compra dos equipamentos e o escopo do piloto. Surge a ideia de um modo sem internet. O piloto é reduzido.
keyPoints: A entrega dos tablets completos ainda não aconteceu
O piloto passa a ter menos lojas
Proposta de um modo sem internet no aplicativo
O seguro dos equipamentos segue sem resposta
decisions: Piloto reduzido para uma loja, a do Centro

actions.task: Cobrar a seguradora sobre o seguro dos tablets

openQuestions: Quem paga o seguro dos tablets?

say.text: Pessoal, tenho um problema. Os 18 tablets chegaram sem o suporte de moto, e o fornecedor só entrega os suportes em 9 de dezembro.
Sem suporte não dá para usar na moto. Isso atrasa tudo?
Atrasa o piloto em três lojas. Eu proponho começar só com a loja do Centro.
Concordo. Uma loja só também reduz o risco.
Então piloto só no Centro por enquanto.
Outra coisa. Eu quero que o aplicativo funcione offline. Sem esse modo eu não aprovo a entrada nas lojas.
Por que offline? Qual é o problema?
Eu explico melhor na próxima, preciso dos números primeiro.
E o seguro? Eu liguei para a seguradora e ainda não tenho resposta.
Heitor, cobra de novo, por favor.
Vou cobrar essa semana.
O treinamento dos motoboys eu deixo com o Rogério, certo?
Isso, eu falo com o líder dos motoboys.
Posso ver o contrato com o fornecedor? Quero conferir as multas.
Mando hoje por e-mail.
Fechado. A gente se encontra daqui a dez dias.

meetings.title: Orçamento e conectividade
meetings.overview: O grupo discute o motivo do modo sem internet e o orçamento. Uma parte do orçamento está parada. O piloto é ampliado.
keyPoints: O modo sem internet ganha apoio com dados
Parte do orçamento aguarda uma etapa externa
O piloto é ampliado para mais uma loja
O seguro dos tablets continua sem solução
decisions: Piloto em duas lojas: Centro e Vila Nova
Modo offline entra como requisito do piloto

actions.task: Pedir ao fornecedor uma data para o modo offline
Cobrar a seguradora sobre o seguro dos tablets

openQuestions: Quem faz o laudo dos tablets?
Quem paga o seguro dos tablets?

say.text: Trouxe os números do offline. Em 22 por cento das entregas do bairro da Serra o celular fica sem sinal, e o motoboy perde a rota.
Isso é muita coisa. Então o offline vira requisito.
Sim, e é por isso que eu insisti nesse ponto. Vou pedir ao fornecedor uma data.
Tenho uma notícia ruim. O orçamento de equipamentos está congelado até a auditoria de 15 de janeiro.
Então não dá para comprar nada novo antes disso.
Só o que já foi pedido. Os 18 tablets já estavam pagos.
Com os tablets pagos, eu consigo montar duas lojas. Centro e Vila Nova.
Então o piloto vai para duas lojas.
E o seguro. A seguradora quer um laudo de cada tablet, e o valor segurado seria 1.900 reais por tablet.
Quem faz o laudo?
Ninguém sabe ainda. O fornecedor diz que não faz.
Então continua em aberto.
Eu preciso também de uma data para o modo offline. Sem isso o piloto não vale.
Cobra o fornecedor, Cássia.
Cobro hoje.
Eu sigo com a seguradora.

meetings.title: Revisão do piloto e troca de fornecedor
meetings.overview: A equipe revisa o calendário e o contrato. O projeto muda de fornecedor, de patrocinador e de data. Um ponto sobre o seguro continua aberto.
keyPoints: Nova data para o início do piloto
Mudança de fornecedor e de custo mensal
O treinamento dos motoboys depende de terceiros
decisions: Fornecedor passa a ser a Trilhar
Início do piloto em 21 de março

actions.task: Assinar o contrato com a Trilhar
Enviar o aviso formal aos motoboys
Cobrar a seguradora sobre o seguro dos tablets

openQuestions: Quem faz o laudo dos tablets?

say.text: Pessoal, mudança grande. A RotaViva só entrega o modo offline em junho, então a gente vai para a Trilhar.
A Trilhar já tem offline pronto. Eu testei uma semana, e funcionou bem na Serra.
O custo é 6.800 reais por mês, bem mais caro que os 4.200 da RotaViva.
Aceito o custo, porque offline é requisito. Outra mudança: o Heitor assume como patrocinador do projeto, e eu fico com as operações novas.
Combinado, eu assumo.
E a data do piloto? Com a troca eu só consigo 21 de março.
Tudo bem. Mas ainda tem o treinamento dos motoboys.
O sindicato pediu um aviso formal com 30 dias de antecedência para mudar o sistema de rotas. Então o treinamento só pode começar depois.
Então o aviso precisa sair já.
Eu mando o aviso amanhã.
Sobre o seguro, ainda nada. A seguradora aceita o laudo de qualquer perito, mas ninguém contratou um.
Então continua aberto.
Eu também preciso de um contrato novo com a Trilhar.
Eu assino na semana que vem.
Combinado.

meetings.title: Warehouse migration kickoff
meetings.overview: The team plans to move analytics from the old warehouse to a cloud one. They fix a cutover date, an owner and a log policy.
keyPoints: Move from Datamere to Pellucid planned
Raw logs kept for a short period
decisions: Cutover on 15 February
Keep raw logs for 90 days

actions.task: Count the dashboards that use custom functions

say.text: Welcome. We move our analytics from Datamere to Pellucid.
Leopold, you own the contract, right?
Yes, I own the contract and I lead the migration.
What is the target date for the cutover?
15 February. That is before the finance quarter close.
I need to know where the data lives. Is it all in one region?
For now, yes. Pellucid has a Dublin region available today.
I will check the rules. What about the logs?
We keep raw logs for 90 days. After that they are deleted.
Ninety days is short for the finance team, but fine for a start.
Support tier: we take the basic tier. It costs 18k per month in total with storage.
Basic support has no phone line. Is that a problem?
Not for now. We can upgrade later.
I will count the dashboards that use custom SQL functions. Those are the hard part.
Good. Priyanka, please draft a data map.
Yes, by next week.

meetings.title: Dashboards and security ideas
meetings.overview: Sunniva reports on the dashboard work. The team talks about log retention and an encryption idea. The cutover plan stays under review.
keyPoints: Dashboard rewrite is only partly done
A new encryption idea is raised
decisions: Keep raw logs for 180 days

actions.task: Rewrite the dashboards that use custom functions

openQuestions: Do we need encryption for sensitive tables?

say.text: I counted. Fourteen finance dashboards use a custom SQL function. I rewrote only 9 of 23 queries behind them so far.
That is slow. Can the function be copied into Pellucid?
Not as is. The syntax is different, so every query needs a manual change.
Finance told me they want raw logs for longer, for audits.
Then we extend retention. I propose 180 days.
That works for audits.
Another point. I want column-level encryption for sensitive tables. We should plan it now.
Why now? It adds work to the cutover.
I will bring details next time. I just want it on the list.
Okay, it goes on the list as a proposal.
Is the data map ready?
Yes, I sent it yesterday.
Thanks. I will test the nightly load time this week.
Should we move the cutover date?
Not yet. We wait for the load test.
Fine.

meetings.title: Security review and region
meetings.overview: Priyanka reports on the security review. A region rule is discussed, and the encryption proposal is approved. The cutover date moves.
decisions: Column-level encryption is required for sensitive tables
Move the cutover date to 9 April

actions.task: Rewrite the dashboards that use custom functions
Ask Pellucid about the Frankfurt region

openQuestions: Can Datamere give a short extension?

say.text: The security review is done. First, the encryption. The October audit found three tables with national ids in plain text. That is why I want column-level encryption.
Priyanka, three tables is serious. Approved, we do it.
Does this slow the dashboards?
A little, but the finance queries only read masked values.
Second, the region. Our rules say data must stay in the Frankfurt region.
I told you Dublin earlier. I need to ask Pellucid.
They offer Frankfurt only from 12 March, so we cannot cut over before that.
Then 15 February is dead. I propose 9 April.
April is better for me too. The dashboard rewrite goes slowly.
Okay, the new date is 9 April.
I will keep rewriting. Thirteen of 23 are done now.
We should also think about the Datamere license. It ends soon.
What is the end date?
It renews on 1 April, and the notice period is 60 days.
Then we are already past the notice date for an exit.
Yes. I will ask Datamere for a short extension, but I have no price yet.
Keep me posted.

meetings.title: Load time and plan review
meetings.overview: The group reviews load performance and the plan. The migration changes owner and support tier. The old license question is still open.
decisions: Keep raw logs for 120 days with an archive after that
Upgrade to the premium support tier

actions.task: Get a price for the Datamere extension

openQuestions: What does the Datamere extension cost?

say.text: The nightly load takes 7 hours, and our limit is 4. So the finance dashboards cannot go live on the new warehouse yet.
Which part is slow?
The join on the orders table. I will try partitioning.
Costs went up too. Encryption and the extra storage push us above plan.
Retention at 180 days is expensive. I propose 120 days, and an archive after that.
An archive is fine for audits.
Agreed.
Also, the basic support tier is not enough. We had two incidents last week and no phone line.
So we upgrade to premium. The monthly cost goes from 18k to 26k.
Right. And I will step back from migration lead. I move to the platform team, and Sunniva takes over.
Okay, I accept. I need Priyanka's help for the dashboards.
Sure.
Seventeen of 23 are done.
Last point: the Datamere license. It renews on 1 April.
Did you get a price for the extension?
No. Datamere will not give a price before 20 March.
So we cannot plan the budget.
Correct. It stays open.
